questions.question: A bank teller sees only account balances and customer names, while the DBA sees the entire database structure. Which ANSI/SPARC level defines the teller's customized view?
questions.explanation: The external level holds the individual user views; each user group sees only the portion of the database relevant to it, unlike the shared conceptual level beneath.

questions.question: The team takes a finished ER diagram and rewrites it as relational schemas with tables, keys, and constraints — still without choosing Oracle, MySQL, or any specific DBMS product. Which design phase are they performing?
questions.explanation: Logical design maps the conceptual schema into a chosen data model (relational here) but stays independent of a specific DBMS; physical design comes after a DBMS is picked.

questions.question: Adding a new column to the STUDENTS table and reordering its columns must not force a rewrite of the registrar's existing views. Which independence property protects the views?
questions.explanation: Logical data independence lets the conceptual schema evolve — new attributes, entities, or relationships — without changing the external views built on it.

questions.question: Before executing a query, the DBMS looks up each table's columns, data types, constraints, and granted privileges in its own internal metadata store. What is this store called?
questions.explanation: The data dictionary (system catalog) stores metadata — schema descriptions, users, privileges, statistics — which the DBMS consults for every operation.

questions.question: After a power failure kills the server mid-transaction, the DBMS replays the log on restart to redo committed changes and undo incomplete ones. Which component performs this work?
questions.explanation: The recovery manager uses the transaction log (and backups) to bring the database back to a consistent state after crashes or media failures.

questions.question: An INSERT is rejected because the new EMPLOYEE row's EmpID duplicates a key value already in the table. Which constraint type did the DBMS enforce?
questions.explanation: The uniqueness (key) constraint forbids duplicate values in key columns; it underlies primary key enforcement and rejected the duplicate EmpID.

questions.question: A 1960s IBM application stores records as a tree in which every child segment has exactly one parent segment, and programs navigate by following parent-child pointers. Which data model is this?
questions.explanation: The hierarchical model organizes records into trees of parent-child (1:N) segments — the structure behind IMS — preceding the network and relational models.

questions.question: For a two-table join, the DBMS estimates the cost of a nested-loop plan versus a hash-join plan and executes the cheaper one. Which component made this choice?
questions.explanation: The query optimizer enumerates candidate execution plans, estimates their costs from catalog statistics, and selects the plan expected to be cheapest.

questions.question: To avoid repeated disk reads, the DBMS keeps recently used pages in a reserved area of main memory and serves repeated requests for them from there. What is this memory structure called?
questions.explanation: The buffer pool (buffer cache) holds disk pages in memory; hits avoid disk I/O, and dirty pages are written back under the buffer manager's policy.

questions.question: The DBA moves a table's files to a faster disk array and changes the file organization and indexing method, yet no table definition or user view needs modification. Which independence permits this?
questions.explanation: Physical data independence shields the logical schema from changes to storage structures — file organization, indexes, or devices — via the conceptual/internal mapping.

questions.question: One schema describes every entity, attribute, and relationship for the whole organization — above physical storage details, yet shared by all the individual user views. Which ANSI/SPARC level is it?
questions.explanation: The conceptual level is the single community-wide logical description of all data; external views sit above it and the internal storage description sits below.

questions.question: A clerk's view must be reformulated, so only the description of how her view derives from the global logical schema is updated. What is that link called?
questions.explanation: Each external view is tied to the conceptual schema by an external/conceptual mapping; adjusting it preserves logical data independence when either side changes.

questions.question: Analysts interview departments and produce an ER diagram of entities, attributes, and relationships before any data model or DBMS is chosen. Which design phase produced this diagram?
questions.explanation: Conceptual design captures the requirements in a high-level model such as ER; it precedes logical design (which picks a data model) and physical design (which picks a DBMS).

questions.question: An INSERT of an ORDER_LINES row is blocked because it references an ORDERS row that does not exist. Which DBMS subsystem enforces such declared integrity rules?
questions.explanation: The integrity manager checks stored data against declared constraints — key, entity, and referential integrity — and rejects operations like this orphaned insert.

questions.question: A business analyst bypasses the canned reports and types ad-hoc SELECT statements directly into the DBMS query interface herself. Which category of database user is she?
questions.explanation: Sophisticated users — analysts, scientists, engineers — interact directly with the query language, unlike naive users who rely on canned transactions.

questions.question: A COBOL application embeds SQL statements directly in its source code. Which DBMS component extracts the embedded SQL calls from the host-language program so the host compiler can process the rest?
questions.explanation: The DML precompiler scans the host program, extracts embedded DML commands, and replaces them with calls to DBMS code before host-language compilation.

questions.question: When a CREATE TABLE statement is submitted, which DBMS component processes it and stores the new table's description into the catalog?
questions.explanation: The DDL compiler processes schema definitions and stores the resulting metadata descriptions in the DBMS catalog.

questions.question: A legacy system organizes records into owner-member SET types and requires programs to follow currency pointers to navigate between related records. Which database model is this?
questions.explanation: The network (CODASYL DBTG) model represents data as record types linked by owner-member set types navigated via currency pointers.

questions.question: Which category of database worker determines the requirements of end users — especially naive users — and develops specifications for the canned transactions that application programmers then implement?
questions.explanation: System analysts gather end-user requirements and specify canned transactions; application programmers implement and test them.

questions.question: A GIS application needs to store polygons as user-defined types with methods and inheritance inside otherwise ordinary relational tables. Which data model extends the relational model with these object-oriented features?
questions.explanation: The object-relational model embeds object-oriented features — user-defined types, methods, and inheritance — into the relational model.
